headings.title: Elements of offense of bigamy by married person
headings.reviewNote: Defines bigamy as married person purporting to marry another or cohabiting under bigamous marriage entered into in another jurisdiction.

headings.title: Reasonable belief of legal eligibility to remarry exception
headings.reviewNote: Provides that married person does not commit bigamy if person reasonably believes they are legally eligible to remarry.

headings.title: Defendant burden of injecting reasonable belief of eligibility to remarry
headings.reviewNote: Places burden of injecting issue of reasonable belief of eligibility to remarry upon defendant.

headings.title: Elements of offense of bigamy by unmarried person
headings.reviewNote: Defines bigamy as unmarried person purporting to marry another knowing other is married, or cohabiting under bigamous marriage entered into in another jurisdiction.

headings.title: Class A misdemeanor classification
headings.reviewNote: Classifies offense of bigamy as a class A misdemeanor.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified against archived text; aligned subsection 4 note with statutory 'another jurisdiction' wording.

headings.title: Definition and elements of offense of incest
headings.reviewNote: Defines incest as marrying, purporting to marry, or engaging in sexual intercourse or deviate sexual intercourse with specified blood, adoptive, stepchild, or collateral relatives.

headings.title: Class E felony classification
headings.reviewNote: Classifies offense of incest as a class E felony.

headings.title: Probation prohibition for repeat incest offenders
headings.reviewNote: Bars court from granting probation to person previously found guilty of incest.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified against archived text; corrected subsection 1 note to remove fabricated 'cohabiting' and reflect marrying, purporting to marry, sexual intercourse, and deviate sexual intercourse.

headings.title: Definition and elements of abandonment of a child in the first degree
headings.reviewNote: Defines offense as parent, guardian, or custodian leaving child under four with purpose wholly to abandon under circumstances likely to result in serious physical injury or death.

headings.title: Offense classification and penalty enhancement for child death
headings.reviewNote: Classifies offense as class B felony, or class A felony if child dies.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified against archived text; tightened subsection 1 note to 'serious physical injury or death'.

headings.title: Definition and elements of abandonment of a child in the second degree
headings.reviewNote: Defines offense as parent, guardian, or custodian leaving child under eight with purpose wholly to abandon under circumstances likely to result in serious physical injury or death.

headings.title: Offense classification and penalty enhancements for serious physical injury or death
headings.reviewNote: Classifies offense as class D felony, class B felony if child suffers serious physical injury, or class A felony if child dies.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified against archived text; tightened subsection 2 heading to specify 'serious physical injury or death'.

headings.title: Definition and elements of offense of criminal nonsupport
headings.reviewNote: Defines offense as knowingly failing to provide adequate support for spouse, or parent knowingly failing to provide legally obligated support for unemancipated child or stepchild.

headings.title: Statutory definitions and nonmedical remedial treatment exclusion
headings.reviewNote: Defines arrearage, child, good cause, and support, and recognizes nonmedical remedial treatment.

headings.title: Affirmative defense of inability to support for good cause
headings.reviewNote: Establishes inability to support for good cause as affirmative defense proved by defendant by preponderance of evidence.

headings.title: Defendant burden of injecting nonmedical remedial treatment issue
headings.reviewNote: Places burden of injecting issue of nonmedical remedial treatment upon defendant.

headings.title: Offense classification and twelve-month aggregate arrearage felony threshold
headings.reviewNote: Classifies offense as class A misdemeanor, or class E felony if total arrearage exceeds twelve monthly court-ordered payments.

headings.title: Probation and parole support conditions, revocation, and conviction expungement
headings.reviewNote: Permits ordering current support and arrearage payments as probation or parole condition and revoking probation or parole absent good cause; governs felony criminal nonsupport expungement.

headings.title: Work release eligibility during incarceration to satisfy support obligations
headings.reviewNote: Permits placing nonviolent incarcerated offender on work release if meeting department of corrections criteria to satisfy support obligations, with arrearages satisfied per collection agreement.

headings.title: Parole or work release consideration for first- and second-time offenders
headings.reviewNote: Permits parole or work release consideration for nonviolent first- and second-time nonsupport offenders.

headings.title: Quarterly reporting by prosecuting attorneys on IV-D child support cases
headings.reviewNote: Requires prosecuting attorneys in cooperative counties to report IV-D charges and convictions quarterly to family support division.

headings.title: Venue and prosecution in county of child or defendant residence
headings.reviewNote: Requires persons accused of nonsupport of a child to be prosecuted in any county where the child or defendant resided during the charged period.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified against archived text; updated subsection 2 heading to reflect nonmedical remedial treatment exclusion, preserved permissive 'may' in subsections 6-8, and corrected subsection 10 note to mandatory 'shall be prosecuted'.

headings.title: Definition and elements of endangering the welfare of a child in the first degree
headings.reviewNote: Defines offense as knowingly creating substantial risk to child under eighteen, custodial sexual conduct, encouraging chapter 571 or 579 violations, or unlawful manufacture, possession, sale, or related acts involving fentanyl, carfentanil, amphetamine, methamphetamine, or analogues in child's presence or residence.

headings.title: Felony classification and enhanced penalties for pattern, repeat offense, drugs, injury, or death
headings.reviewNote: Classifies offense as class D felony, class C felony for pattern, physical injury, or repeat offense, class B felony with five-year minimum for fentanyl or carfentanil or for serious physical injury, or class A felony for death.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified against archived text (2026 merged amendment); updated subsection 2 heading and notes to include repeat offense enhancement, carfentanil/analogues, and five-year minimum for fentanyl/carfentanil.

headings.title: Definition and elements of endangering the welfare of a child in the second degree
headings.reviewNote: Defines offense as criminal negligence creating risk to child under seventeen, juvenile court delinquency, custody neglect, or drug nuisance entry.

headings.title: Nonmedical remedial treatment exception
headings.reviewNote: Provides that welfare of child is not endangered solely because nonmedical remedial treatment recognized by Missouri law is provided.

headings.title: Offense classification and pattern of activity enhancement
headings.reviewNote: Classifies offense as class A misdemeanor, or class E felony if committed as part of prescribed pattern of activity by two or more persons.

headings.title: Definitions of statutory terms for abuse or neglect of a child
headings.reviewNote: Defines abuse, abusive head trauma, mental injury, neglect, physical injury, serious emotional injury, and serious physical injury.

headings.title: Knowing abuse or neglect of a child elements
headings.reviewNote: Defines offense as knowingly causing child under eighteen to suffer physical or mental injury or placing child in harmful situation.

headings.title: Recklessly causing abusive head trauma to a child
headings.reviewNote: Defines offense as recklessly causing child under eighteen to suffer from abusive head trauma.

headings.title: Safe harbor for delivery of child to emergency services provider
headings.reviewNote: Provides that delivery of child to emergency services provider does not constitute abuse or neglect.

headings.title: Safe harbor for child's participation in independent activities without adult supervision
headings.reviewNote: Provides that allowing child of appropriate age and maturity to engage in independent activities without supervision is not abuse or neglect.

headings.title: Felony classification, mandatory minimum terms, and penalty enhancements
headings.reviewNote: Classifies offense as class D felony with one-year minimum without probation, parole, or conditional release (in version in effect until 1-01-28), class B felony with five-year minimum for repeat or serious injury, or class A felony for child death.

headings.title: Enhanced class A felony tier for sexual abuse or exploitation of child under fourteen
headings.reviewNote: Classifies offense as class A felony with fifteen-year minimum without probation, parole, or conditional release for serious emotional or physical injury to child under fourteen from sexual abuse under section 566.100 or sexual exploitation under section 573.023.

headings.title: Prosecuting attorney authority to refer suspect to treatment or counseling agency
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes circuit or prosecuting attorney to refer suspect to consenting treatment agency without limiting prosecution discretion.

headings.title: Proof of every element beyond a reasonable doubt preserved
headings.reviewNote: Affirms that every element of any referred crime must be proven beyond a reasonable doubt.

headings.title: Reasonable discipline and spanking exception
headings.reviewNote: Provides that discipline, including spanking administered in a reasonable manner, shall not be construed to be abuse under this section.

entries.reviewSummary: Dual-version entry (H.B. 737 & 486, 2025; Revisor note states in effect until 1-01-28); retains one-year minimum on class D felony in subsection 6(1); broadened subsection 7 heading to include sexual exploitation under section 573.023 and removed 'parental' narrowing in subsection 10.

headings.title: Definitions of statutory terms for abuse or neglect of a child
headings.reviewNote: Defines abuse, abusive head trauma, mental injury, neglect, physical injury, serious emotional injury, and serious physical injury.

headings.title: Knowing abuse or neglect of a child elements
headings.reviewNote: Defines offense as knowingly causing child under eighteen to suffer physical or mental injury or placing child in harmful situation.

headings.title: Recklessly causing abusive head trauma to a child
headings.reviewNote: Defines offense as recklessly causing child under eighteen to suffer from abusive head trauma.

headings.title: Safe harbor for delivery of child to emergency services provider
headings.reviewNote: Provides that delivery of child to emergency services provider does not constitute abuse or neglect.

headings.title: Safe harbor for child's participation in independent activities without adult supervision
headings.reviewNote: Provides that allowing child of appropriate age and maturity to engage in independent activities without supervision is not abuse or neglect.

headings.title: Felony classification, five-year minimum for class B, and penalty enhancements
headings.reviewNote: Classifies offense as class D felony without the one-year minimum (in version effective 1-01-28), class B felony with five-year minimum for repeat or serious injury, or class A felony for child death.

headings.title: Enhanced class A felony tier for sexual abuse or exploitation of child under fourteen
headings.reviewNote: Classifies offense as class A felony with fifteen-year minimum without probation, parole, or conditional release for serious emotional or physical injury to child under fourteen from sexual abuse under section 566.100 or sexual exploitation under section 573.023.

headings.title: Prosecuting attorney authority to refer suspect to treatment or counseling agency
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes circuit or prosecuting attorney to refer suspect to consenting treatment agency without limiting prosecution discretion.

headings.title: Proof of every element beyond a reasonable doubt preserved
headings.reviewNote: Affirms that every element of any referred crime must be proven beyond a reasonable doubt.

headings.title: Reasonable discipline and spanking exception
headings.reviewNote: Provides that discipline, including spanking administered in a reasonable manner, shall not be construed to be abuse under this section.

entries.reviewSummary: Dual-version entry (H.B. 2637 & 3155, 2026; Revisor note states effective 1-01-28); removes one-year minimum on class D felony in subsection 6(1) while keeping five-year class B minimum; broadened subsection 7 heading to include section 573.023 and removed 'parental' narrowing in subsection 10.

headings.title: Definition and elements of female genital mutilation
headings.reviewNote: Defines offense as excising or infibulating genitalia of female child under seventeen, or parent or guardian permitting procedure.

headings.title: Class B felony classification
headings.reviewNote: Classifies offense of genital mutilation as a class B felony.

headings.title: Inapplicability of custom, ritual, or consent as affirmative defense
headings.reviewNote: Provides that custom, ritual, standard practice, or consent by the child, parent, or legal guardian is not an affirmative defense.

headings.title: Defense for medically necessary procedure by licensed physician
headings.reviewNote: Provides defense for conduct performed by a licensed Missouri physician when necessary to preserve the child's health or for medical purposes connected with labor or birth.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified against archived text; broadened subsection 3 heading to cover child or parental/guardian consent and removed unstated 'surgical' narrowing from subsection 4 heading.

headings.title: Definition and elements of unlawful transactions with a child
headings.reviewNote: Defines offense as pawnbroker, junk dealer, secondhand dealer, or employee buying non-agricultural property from unemancipated minor without written parental consent, permitting minor in controlled substance premises, or selling explosives (<17) or fireworks (<14) without written parental consent.

headings.title: Class B misdemeanor classification
headings.reviewNote: Classifies offense of unlawful transactions with a child as a class B misdemeanor.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified against archived text (2025 amendment); expanded subsection 1 note to cover junk/secondhand dealers, agricultural exception, and written parental consent.

headings.title: Definition and elements of trafficking in children
headings.reviewNote: Defines offense as offering, giving, receiving, or soliciting money or consideration for delivery of child for adoption, consent to adopt, waiver of consent, or consent to termination of parental rights.

headings.title: Exception for consideration or conduct permitted under chapter 453
headings.reviewNote: Provides that no offense is committed if the money, consideration, thing of value, or conduct is permitted under chapter 453 relating to adoption.

headings.title: Class D felony classification
headings.reviewNote: Classifies offense of trafficking in children as a class D felony.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified against archived text; broadened subsection 1 heading to encompass parental-rights termination consents and removed unstated 'legal expenses' from subsection 2 heading.
